analysis.title: Korn Ferry (KFY): Investor group meeting with management reinforces Talent Suite differentiation and AMS upside
key_insights: Goldman reiterates Buy on Korn Ferry (KFY) with a 12-month price target of $95 against a $76.29 price (24.5% upside) after a virtual investor group meeting with the CFO, the head of the Global Technology Practice, the head of AI strategy, a solution architect and investor relations.

Goldman came away more positive on Talent Suite differentiation, the AMS combination and the AI strategy. It believes these can support more durable revenue growth, greater revenue visibility and sustained margin expansion.

Talent Suite links job design, workforce assessment and employee development in one workflow. In the demo it defined a key account manager success profile, assessed the existing team across 56 data points, benchmarked the results externally and recommended hiring priorities, development programs and learning content.

AI converts static assessments into continuous development. After a ~45-minute assessment, an AI coach recommended actions, assigned short learning content and generated a 5-7 minute skill simulation with feedback. Recurring assessment, coaching and simulation usage is a path to incremental consumption revenue.

Goldman sees the moat in proprietary data embedded in client workflows. Talent Suite draws on billions of data points, 115mn assessments, 12,000+ defined jobs and compensation data from 30,000+ clients, and feeds its success profiles and benchmarks into clients' existing HCM and performance management systems, which should raise client embeddedness.

Talent Suite has ten modules, so clients can start with one use case (job architecture, assessments, compensation benchmarking or development) and expand. KFY said a full deployment for an organization of ~50,000 employees could be roughly $6-8mn of total contract value for the software subscription, with consulting sold in addition.

The AMS acquisition adds RPO, contingent workforce solutions, early-career and campus recruiting and talent acquisition technology consulting, with limited overlap with KFY's portfolio. Revenue synergies are slow because these offerings have 12-18 month sales cycles and convert to revenue over 4-5 years, so new business signings are the best near-term indicator.

Deeper client penetration is the largest productivity lever. About 4,500 clients generate ~90% of fee revenue but buy only ~1.5 solutions on average. Average fees rise from ~$170,000 at 1.5 solutions to $350,000 at two, $700,000 at 2.5 and nearly $3mn above 2.5 solutions.

Cost synergies should arrive ahead of revenue synergies. KFY targets AMS run-rate EBITDA of at least $140mn within one year, up from ~$100mn, and said it could hit the target sooner and exceed it. Goldman sees faster realization as near-term estimate upside.

AMS came with ~$650mn of revenue, ~8,000 employees (~6,000 in global capability centers) and ~15% EBITDA margins at closing. Capability center employee cost is roughly 60% of KFY's, which supports shifting more delivery and corporate work to lower-cost locations.
Management indicated the combined company could reach the top of the existing 16-18% EBITDA margin range and potentially progress toward 19-20% over time.
Goldman's model has fee revenue growing 20.5% in FY4/27E to $3,503mn on AMS, then 11.9% in FY4/28E, with adjusted EPS of $5.69 in FY4/27E and $6.32 in FY4/28E.

The $95 target uses 14.5x NTM+1YR EPS of $6.52, a slight discount to the staffing peer median NTM P/E of 14.8x. The discount reflects the pro-cyclical executive search, RPO and professional search and interim businesses, balanced against cross-sell and a diversified mix. Risks cited are macroeconomic headwinds, competition, acquisition integration and FX.

market_movers.rationale: Management meeting reinforced Talent Suite differentiation, AMS cost synergy upside and the AI-enabled delivery strategy. Target of $95 is 24.5% above the $76.29 price.

earnings_insights: KFY FY4/26 (April year-end) adjusted EPS $5.31 reported, adjusted EBITDA $497.8mn and fee revenue $2,907.5mn, per Goldman's model.
KFY first fiscal quarter ended Jul-26 adjusted EPS $1.43 reported, versus Goldman's $1.31 for the year-ago quarter.
Goldman estimates (not reported) adjusted EPS of $1.35 for Oct-26E, $1.39 for Jan-27E and $1.52 for Apr-27E, giving FY4/27E adjusted EPS of $5.69.

Goldman estimates FY4/27E fee revenue of $3,503.3mn (+20.5% y/y) and adjusted EBITDA of $598.1mn, with the step-up driven by the AMS acquisition. Goldman estimates FY4/28E adjusted EPS of $6.32 and FY4/29E of $7.16.
Management target (company, not a Goldman forecast): AMS run-rate EBITDA of at least $140mn within one year of the acquisition, versus ~$100mn at entry.

tension_points.bull_case: Structural advantages from cross-selling and a diversified business mix enable market share gains and more resilient revenue, supported by Talent Suite recurring revenue and AMS cost synergies.
tension_points.bear_case: Pro-cyclical executive search, RPO and professional search and interim businesses justify a slight discount to the 14.8x staffing peer median NTM P/E. Macro, competition, integration and FX are the named risks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: New business signings at AMS and cross-sold accounts failing to build, since the report calls signings the best near-term indicator of revenue synergy progress.

theme_stances.key_argument: Proprietary data and workflow integration should increase client embeddedness and make Talent Suite more difficult to displace.
theme_stances.evidence: Proprietary intelligence embedded in client workflows creates the moat.

theme_stances.key_argument: Faster realization of AMS cost savings could provide near-term estimate upside and a foundation for further margin expansion.
theme_stances.evidence: Cost synergies should materialize ahead of revenue synergies
